prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / stylized-concept.
Create ONE polished landscape target concept board for the EXISTING Highland Citadel scene, based on both provided game screenshots, inspired by Oskar Stålberg's Bad North and Townscaper visual art direction. This is a proposed art target, NOT a screenshot of implemented work.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the user's BACKSIDE screenshot, showing the specific unresolved abrupt green turf patches and sparse vegetation. Image 2 is the FRONT overview and is the PRIMARY layout and architecture reference. Faithfully retain this recognizable place, not a new generic fantasy island.
COMPOSITION: wide 16:9, high-quality stylized 3D game-art rendering. A large front three-quarter aerial overview takes nearly the entire canvas, matching image 2's scene arrangement. One small clearly separated close-up inset in the lower right shows the back mountain vegetation-to-rock transition from image 1, with the intrusive overhead gondola/rope and UI omitted. Small elegant Chinese labels only: top left “高山圣城 · 目标图”, inset “背坡植被过渡”, discreet bottom “概念提案 · 非实机画面”. No extra diagrams, no palette strips.
MUST KEEP: dense old city on the LEFT, its slender tall stone tower with a small terracotta domed crown, compact warm stone houses and terracotta domes; large monumental domed citadel on the RIGHT, broad stepped buttressed stone volumes, teal slate central dome, smaller muted terracotta domes; the EXISTING two settlements separated by the bay and connected by the pedestrian bridge. Preserve the broad foreground curving coastal railway, harbor stairs up to old city, waterfall below old city, sea inlet and canyon opening. Keep original placement, scale hierarchy and original architecture identity. Existing giant mountain shapes and footprint remain recognizable with improved structural transitions. Both castles and mountains fit wholly in frame. Do NOT replace architecture with Northern European cottages or generic medieval pointed-roof castles.
MOUNTAINS: sculpted chalk/limestone highlands, coherent offset main summit, supporting ridges, saddles and broad irregular rock shelves. Clearly legible cliff strata and genuinely thick shoulder volumes, softened convex edges but hard meaningful escarpments. Connect ridges without closing the canyon. Avoid tall paper slabs, stacked cones and incessant crinkly triangulation.
KEY TARGET - VEGETATION TRANSITION: on soil-bearing terraces/shoulders, connected muted sage-green turf cores graduate into patchy short grass and grouped low rounded shrubs, then sparse moss and warm grey exposed soil/gravel, finally pale bare limestone. The irregular margins are small-scale softly scalloped, not whole triangular face cutouts, arrowhead tails or flat dark green stickers. Steep cliff faces remain primarily bare. Some sparse short cypress groups of varied height, with broad irregular bush clumps; no equally spaced rows of spikes, no oversized forest, no floating plants. Every plant visibly rooted. Grass and rock share coherent soft sunlight and contact shading. The inset makes this layered transition unambiguous and buildable.
CASTLE GROUNDING: terraced stone plinths with short retaining walls step naturally into rock shoulders. Low gardens soften selected wall feet. Gate openings, harbor access stairs and railway remain visibly unobstructed; no grass over tracks or castle foundations. Architectural module joins are clean, rounded subtly at exposed corners, solid weight, restrained detail.
STYLE AND COLOUR: Oskar-inspired readable diorama masses, broad harmonious color fields, soft ambient contact shadows, simplified clusters with nuanced normals, crisp yet gently eased silhouette edges. Warm pale ivory limestone lit faces versus desaturated blue-grey shadows, muted sage and olive vegetation with lighter grass tips, grey-brown soil fringe, deep turquoise sea, restrained terracotta and teal roof accents. Airy pale blue daytime sky and a few high soft clouds; enough directional light to explain surface form, no strong sunset tint, no heavy fog hiding joins, no black outlines or wireframe cracks. Preserve a sense of the original small spherical world in the curving foreground coast, without turning it into a floating cutaway island. Render beautiful, achievable GAME ART, not photorealism, not an oil painting.
scope: Concept image only, no runtime code or castle/transport geometry changed. Composition preserves main identities, generated details are proposals not verified geometry.
